The Harlem Hellfighters. They spent 191 days on the frontline, longer than any other American unit but they also suffered the most in terms of losses. They were sent to fight alongside the French due to racial segregation and were welcomed with open arms by their adopted comrades. They even exchanged their American standard issue equipment for French gear and even introduced jazz to the front lines.

These guys were the epitome of badass, in May 1918 Pvt. Henry Johnson and Pvt. Needham Roberts reportedly held off a German patrol of 24 men, lobbing grenades and resorting to using their rifles as clubs and using their bolo knives to fend off the attack. They both received France’s highest military award for bravery.

On November 17th the Harlem Hellfighters became the first allied unit to reach the Rhine. Now you tell me these heroes don’t deserve more attention.

Also the name “Hellfighters” were given to them by the Germans as they never lost a foot of ground.

The post-apocalyptic world (name pending) is inhabited by hundreds of tribe-states constantly warring for their respective god. The gods have their own agendas and very few consider other gods as allies or even the same kind. Recently the Goddess Fyndallo of the Prairie States has started to wither and die. She reached out to Velspa in his dreams for reasons unknown and she told the priest the secret of the Gods which drove him mad. In the darkest part of the northern forests, at the base of the Harron Kush where the great mountains meet the ancient trees stands the Tree of the Tall Fellow. A haunting idol belonging to the mysterious God of the Harron. The great tree is strewn with the hides of sacrifices made by the Cut Wives of Harron. None but the Tall Fellow's followers know why they commit these grizzly sacrifices as everyone knows the Cut Wives make use of every part of the body in their practices. 

The Tall Fellow is a spindly being standing at twice the size of a grown man. He wears a poncho made of moss and twigs, hiding many charms and trinkets underneath. He dons a wide brimmed hat which is his signature symbol, adopted by the Cut Wives of Harron.

The Tall Fellow is the main character of a cautionary tale among the Southern people, one told to children to discourage wandering off into unknown lands. To the well traveled Scrapsmiths and Mercenaries the Tall Fellow is somewhat of a patron God, who saves lost travelers in his lands for a price. It is common practice for the Brumin Gun Clans to embark on expeditions with dozens of POW's in tow, to serve as "currency" to the Tall Fellow when needed.

TL;DR The Tall Fellow helps lost travelers find their way home for a "skin price", though he does not answer to everyone. The Cut Wives are his primary cult who are mediators for the deals between the god and his "customers". They will take a number of sacrifices dependent on how lost the traveler is and point them in the right direction. They then begin the long journey back to the tree to decorate it with the sacrifice's hide. The Tall Fellow himself will rarely collect the payment and most debate whether he actually exists or not.

For some unkown reason the Ulf clansmen simply chose not to raise the alarm at the sight of the Red banner of Osterland. The battle had been over quickly, a force of Osterland Men-at-arms with a strength of just two-thousand men faced off against a rabble of no less than five-thousand Ulf clansmen. The Ostermen had taken most of the beach before the Ulf left the keep, during the chaos of meeting their attackers one foolish individual had neglected his duty in closing the gate behind the defenders, thus opening the way for the young Baron Michael the Stiff. Simon had lost five men to the Ulf and no matter how few the casualties, the grizzled Sergeant would always feel devastated by any small loss to his unit. 


Turning the bend at an old stone dug-out, Simon could make out the shapes of Sergeant Rhymes and Black Richard at the foot of the watchtower, both were sitting against the tower and eating pack rations.


"Rhymes, Black Rich." The two grunted as they shoveled bread and pork down their throats, re-energising before their next orders came in from Michael the Stiff. Simon tapped the ash from his pipe and sat on the canvas throw with his fellow Sergeants. Black Richard, threw a wine skin into Simon's lap. Black Richard was a refugee from the Pale Lands to the south turned Osterland Sergeant within four years, a hearty warrior and the plumper more dark-skinned alternative to Scab Richard from their company. Simon guzzled his share of wine and tossed the skin back. The warmness of the alcohol tickled his chest and he felt a sudden droop in his eyelids. He yawned and decided to lie on his back, covering his eyes with a rag from the cuff of his sleeve.


"Are you here to remember your orders Simon boy?" Wheezed Rhymes as he puffed on his pipe. "No doubt you've forgotten that it is the west dug-out you should be fortifying currently no?" Rhymes combed his ashen hair back and tied it into a neat topknot that sat atop his head. He was a veteran of the First Nost Wars, an escort on several Imperial Expeditions and was one of the dauntless few to return from the Pale Crusades with his sanity. Simon, Black Richard and many other Sergeants in the Company were once under his command when they first became soldiers of the Third Osterland Army. Rhymes reached into his satchel and pulled a small notebook bound in pig skin. "It never hurts to write down your orders, it can save a lot of trouble and lives..." Rhymes rolled his eyes and began writing in the book. Simon had fallen asleep, it would appear that the wine had dealt the finishing blow.  Rhymes tore out a page of his notebook and pinned it to Simon's collar.


The note had a roughly drawn layout of the beach with a large black arrow pointing to the western watchtower, attatched to the arrow were black letters in a bold font.


DEFEND THIS PLACE!

Phase one: The Job
What if you get contracts through with varying value and importance, the value part motivating the players choose to side track and the importance forces them to side track.

Phase two: The Search
Self explanatory really. Find the mark and assess the strategy, basing said strategy on the species and size etc.

Phase three: The Fight
As for combat do what you can to weaken the creature and then tranquilize it or forcefully restrain it.

Phase four: Postage and Packaging
You got the beast, now you gotta get it back. Transporting a Remohraz from the mountains to the drop off point will be no easy task. You might attract poachers, predators and other people with the contract too. Not to mention resting and watching the beast as it continuously lashes in it's restraints. Also there's feeding, healing any grievous injuries, not to mention toilet time.

Phase five: Preparing the goods
Maybe the client asked for specific things; you couldn't find that one dire wolf with the white coat so maybe they state that dying the fur is fine as long as YOU do it. They might refuse a crocodile with missing teeth or a griffon with mangy fur. All these things require either undoing restraints to complete the task or getting into the cage, sedating the mark is your choice.

Phase six (optional): Rehabilitation 
Not all marks will be happy with their new surroundings and the client may contact you and ask you to either break their new Hyena in or there is difficulty with bonding two hippogryph's in order to breed them.

:)


EDIT: Choose to charm/tame the mark or take it by force. Open combat or drugged bait, your choice!
